newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: SACKED NZ HEALTH MINISTER SAYS WEIGHING HIS FUTURE.
newsitem.headline: SACKED NZ HEALTH MINISTER SAYS WEIGHING HIS FUTURE.

text.p: A New Zealand government politician, sacked from his post as a health minister earlier on Thursday, said he would continue to serve in parliament but was considering his options.
Neil Kirton told a news conference that he wanted to talk to "people he cares for" before taking any further action.
Commenting on the move by Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters to dismiss him as Associate Health Minister earlier in the day, he said, "I was effectively sacked for doing my job."
When asked what his options were, he said he had made enough decisions for today.
As Kirton spoke, Prime Minister Jim Bolger was confirming to parliament that the constitution process to complete Kirton's removal from cabinet office had been carried out.
Bolger said he had notified the governor-general of the government's formal decision shortly after Peters had dismissed Kirton as a minister representing his New Zealand First party in government.
Kirton said he stood by the principles of NZ First that had brought him into parliament and the party into government, but alleged Peters had given him an impossible choice.
"Mr Peters essentially offered me the choice or becoming a house-trained neutered National Party poodle -- unable to effectively defend the public health system.
"I rejected such a total breach of the principles that elected me to parliament and New Zealand First to power.
"I intend to go on keeping the faith."
Kirton said it was apparent that there was an agenda of "creeping privatisation" from senior coalition partner National with which he disagreed.
"In time, as the policy around that becomes clear we will see why they wanted me removed," he added.
Kirton said he considered the reasons given by Peters for his sacking to be fabricated.

"Mr Peters informed me that I had been sacked because I gave three pre-arranged media interviews with various radio stations this morning. He also told me that this was in direct contravention of an alleged instruction provided to me last evening.
"There was no such instruction oral or written," he said.
Kirton added he had to fight to preserve the integrity of the coalition agreement from day one.
The latest alleged transgressions by him were only a smokescreen for the real reason he had been removed from the health portfolio, he said.
"I continued to resist the creeping privatisation that was being proposed in governemnt circles on an almost daily basis.
"In vital policy areas I was combatting the vigourous attempts of (Health Minister Bill) English and various health officials to renege on the coalition agreement.
"Their agenda to privatise remains plain."
He said he was removed from the associate health portfolio by Peters and had then resigned himself from his Customs portfolio, and as a member of the executive.
A government source told Reuters that Associate Treasurer Tuariki John Delamere would take up the Customs Minister job.
No decision has been taken on who would take up the vacant associate health minister's position, the source added.
